items.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
items.note: You don't have to have it all figured out. Bring God into every part of your day and let him lead.

items.text: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
items.note: What you let into your heart shapes everything else. Guard it on purpose.

items.text: Commit your deeds to the Lord, and your plans shall succeed.
items.note: Before you start something today, hand it to God. Plans go better with him in them.

items.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but the Lord directs his steps.
items.note: Make your plans, but hold them loosely. God is directing your steps even when things change.

items.text: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
items.note: Real friends show up in the hard seasons too. Be that kind of friend to someone this week.

items.text: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
items.note: A few loyal friends beat a crowd of shallow ones. Invest in the people who stick around.

items.text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
items.note: Good friends make each other better. Look for people who push you toward God, and do the same for them.

items.text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
items.note: You become like the people you spend time with. Choose your circle carefully.

items.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
items.note: When things get heated, a calm answer can stop a fight before it starts.

items.text: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
items.note: Worry weighs a person down, and one kind word can lift them up. You could be that word for someone today.

items.text: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
items.note: Joy is good for you. Laugh, enjoy the good things, and don't let gloom win the day.

items.text: There are many plans in a man’s heart, but the Lord’s counsel will prevail.
items.note: You can make a lot of plans, but God's purpose is the one that lasts. That's good news.

items.text: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
items.note: Being known as honest and kind is worth more than money or followers.

items.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
items.note: Real wisdom starts with taking God seriously. Everything else builds on that.

items.text: For the Lord gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
items.note: If you need wisdom, ask God. He's the one who gives it.

items.text: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it.
items.note: If you can help someone today, don't wait. Do the good thing while you can.

items.text: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
items.note: Wisdom is worth chasing more than anything else. Make it a priority.

items.text: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you. Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.
items.note: Keep your eyes on where you're going. Think about your next step before you take it.

items.text: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
items.note: Living honestly means you never have to look over your shoulder.

items.text: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
items.note: Talking less often means fewer regrets. Sometimes the wise move is to stay quiet.

items.text: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
items.note: Pride sets you up to fall. Humility makes room to grow.

items.text: He who has a generous eye will be blessed; for he shares his food with the poor.
items.note: Generous people are blessed. Share what you have with someone who needs it.

items.text: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.
items.note: Being corrected stings, but it's how you get better. Don't run from it.

items.text: There is one who speaks rashly like the piercing of a sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
items.note: Words can cut or heal. Choose the ones that heal.

items.text: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who do the truth are his delight.
items.note: God loves it when you're honest, even when a lie would be easier.

items.text: He who guards his mouth guards his soul. One who opens wide his lips comes to ruin.
items.note: Watching what you say keeps you out of a lot of trouble.

items.text: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
items.note: Being slow to get angry is a real strength, not a weakness.

items.text: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
items.note: Peace on the inside is good for you, and envy eats you up. Let comparison go.

items.text: A glad heart makes a cheerful face; but an aching heart breaks the spirit.
items.note: What's going on inside you shows on your face. Take care of your heart.

items.text: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
items.note: Big decisions go better when you ask for advice. You don't have to figure it all out alone.

items.text: The light of the eyes rejoices the heart. Good news gives health to the bones.
items.note: A smile and some good news can change someone's whole day. Share both.

items.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
items.note: Pride usually comes right before a fall. Stay humble and teachable.

items.text: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
items.note: Kind words are sweet and actually help people heal. Say one out loud today.

items.text: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
items.note: Controlling your temper takes more strength than winning a fight.

items.text: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
items.note: Letting something go can save a friendship. Not every offense needs a replay.

items.text: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.
items.note: Staying calm and choosing your words carefully is what wise people do.

items.text: The Lord’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
items.note: When life feels like too much, run to God. He's a safe place.

items.text: He who gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
items.note: Listen to the whole story before you answer. It saves a lot of embarrassment.

items.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
items.note: Your words have real power. Use them to build people up.

items.text: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
items.note: Overlooking an offense isn't weakness. It's wisdom, and it looks good on you.

items.text: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
items.note: Take advice and be open to correction. It's how you get wiser over time.

items.text: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; but every fool will be quarreling.
items.note: Walking away from a fight is honorable. Only fools keep it going.

items.text: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for the Lord, and he will save you.
items.note: You don't have to get even. Trust God to make things right.

items.text: Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.
items.note: Guarding your mouth guards you from a lot of trouble.

items.text: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man, and don’t associate with one who harbors anger: lest you learn his ways, and ensnare your soul.
items.note: Hanging around angry people rubs off on you. Choose friends who bring peace.

items.text: For a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
items.note: Falling down isn't the end. The righteous get back up, again and again.

items.text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
items.note: The right words at the right time are beautiful. Think about timing too.

items.text: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
items.note: Self-control is like walls around a city. Without it, anything can get in.

items.text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
items.note: Drama dies when nobody feeds it. Don't pass the gossip on.

items.text: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
items.note: Tomorrow isn't promised. Do what matters today.

items.text: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
items.note: Let your actions speak. You don't need to hype yourself up.

items.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
items.note: When you're living right, you can face things boldly.

items.text: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
items.note: Hiding your mistakes keeps you stuck. Owning them opens the door to mercy.

items.text: A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings himself under control.
items.note: Saying everything you feel the second you feel it rarely helps. Wise people hold back.

items.text: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the Lord is kept safe.
items.note: Worrying about what people think is a trap. Trusting God sets you free.

items.text: Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
items.note: God's words are true and you can count on them. He protects people who trust him.

items.text: Don’t let kindness and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the tablet of your heart. So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
items.note: Keep kindness and truth close, like something you wear every day.

items.text: My son, don’t despise the Lord’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof: for whom the Lord loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
items.note: When God corrects you, it's because he loves you, like a good father.

items.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
items.note: The ant works hard without anyone making it. Get ahead on what needs doing.

items.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
items.note: Knowing God is where real understanding begins.

items.text: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
items.note: Hate keeps fights going. Love covers a lot of wrongs.

items.text: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
items.note: Being trustworthy means keeping secrets that aren't yours to share.

items.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
items.note: Thinking you're always right is a trap. Wise people listen to advice.

items.text: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
items.note: Wishing for something isn't the same as working for it. Put in the effort.

items.text: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
items.note: Waiting a long time is hard, and it's okay to feel that. A hope fulfilled brings new life.

items.text: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
items.note: What feels right isn't always right. Check your path against God's ways.

items.text: Better is little, with the fear of the Lord, than great treasure with trouble.
items.note: A little with God is better than a lot with stress. Peace is worth more than stuff.

items.text: He who heeds the Word finds prosperity. Whoever trusts in the Lord is blessed.
items.note: Paying attention to wise teaching and trusting God leads to good things.

items.text: He who has pity on the poor lends to the Lord; he will reward him.
items.note: Helping someone in need is like lending to God himself. He notices.

items.text: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.
items.note: Even young people are known by what they do. Your actions tell your story.

items.text: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
items.note: Go after what's right and kind, and you'll find real life along the way.

items.text: Don’t let your heart envy sinners; but rather fear the Lord all day long. Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
items.note: Don't envy people who seem to get away with wrong. Stay close to God. Your future is secure.

items.text: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
items.note: Hard days test your strength. Lean on God and keep going.

items.text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
items.note: A friend who tells you the hard truth is a real friend.

items.text: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
items.note: Your gut isn't always right. Walk in wisdom instead.

items.text: My son, if sinners entice you, don’t consent.
items.note: When people pressure you to do wrong, you can say no. That's real courage.

items.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day.
items.note: Following God is like the sunrise. The path keeps getting brighter.

items.text: I love those who love me. Those who seek me diligently will find me.
items.note: Wisdom isn't hiding from you. Look for it and you'll find it.

items.text: In the fear of the Lord is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.
items.note: Respecting God gives you a strong place to stand, and a safe place for the people you love.

items.text: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear the Lord, and depart from evil. It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.
items.note: Don't think you've got it all figured out. Honor God and turn from wrong. It's good for your whole self.

items.text: For wisdom will enter into your heart. Knowledge will be pleasant to your soul. Discretion will watch over you. Understanding will keep you.
items.note: When wisdom gets into your heart, it protects you and keeps you on track.

items.text: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
items.note: Effort pays off. Lazy habits cost more than they look like they will.

items.text: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
items.note: Being kind to others is good for you too.

items.text: The fear of the Lord teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.
items.note: Humility comes before honor. Stay low and let God lift you up.

items.text: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
items.note: Wisdom is worth more than gold. Spend your time on what really lasts.

items.text: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge; nor being hasty with one’s feet and missing the way.
items.note: Rushing without thinking leads to mistakes. Slow down and think it through.

items.text: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the hearts.
items.note: You can always justify yourself, but God sees your heart. Be honest with yourself.

items.text: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
items.note: Get really good at what you do. Hard work and skill open doors.

items.text: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate. Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.
items.note: Speak up for people who can't speak up for themselves. Stand with them.

items.text: A man’s steps are from the Lord; how then can man understand his way?
items.note: You don't always see where life is going, but God is guiding your steps.

items.text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven.
items.note: There's a right time for everything. If this season is hard, it won't last forever.

items.text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
items.note: Life is better together. When you fall, a friend helps you up. Be that friend too.

items.text: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
items.note: Alone you can be overpowered, but together you're strong. Don't do life solo.

items.text: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
items.note: Finishing well matters more than starting fast. Be patient and don't let anger take over.

items.text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
items.note: Whatever you're doing today, give it your all.

items.text: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them”.
items.note: Don't wait until you're older to follow God. Now is the best time.

items.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
items.note: God makes things beautiful in their time. You don't have to see the whole picture yet.

items.text: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
items.note: Don't rush your words, even with God. Think before you speak.

items.text: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
items.note: If you wait for perfect conditions, you'll never start. Take the step.

items.text: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
items.note: After everything, it comes down to this: honor God and do what he says.

items.text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
items.note: Hard times aren't wasted. God uses them to make you strong and complete.

items.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him.
items.note: If you don't know what to do, ask God. He gives wisdom generously and doesn't make you feel dumb for asking.

items.text: Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those who love him.
items.note: Hanging in there through temptation is worth it. God has something great waiting.

items.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, nor turning shadow.
items.note: Every good thing in your life is a gift from God, and he never changes.

items.text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
items.note: Listen first, talk second, and don't let anger drive. That's how you live God's way.

items.text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
items.note: Don't just hear God's word. Do something with it today.

items.text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
items.note: God's wisdom is peaceful, gentle and fair. That's what it looks like up close.

items.text: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
items.note: Push back against temptation and move toward God. He comes close to you.

items.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
items.note: Stay humble before God, and he will lift you up.

items.text: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
items.note: Be honest with someone you trust, and pray for each other. Prayer is powerful.

items.text: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
items.note: Faith shows up in what you do. Let your actions match what you believe.

items.text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.
items.note: Show your wisdom by how you live, with humility, not by how much you talk.

items.text: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers; but his delight is in the Lord’s law. On his law he meditates day and night. He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.
items.note: Stay rooted in God's word and you'll grow like a healthy tree, even in dry seasons.

items.text: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, Lord, my rock, and my redeemer.
items.note: A good prayer for today: may my words and my thoughts please God.

items.text: Show me your ways, Lord. Teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth, and teach me, For you are the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.
items.note: It's okay to ask God to show you the way. He loves to teach you.

items.text: Wait for the Lord. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for the Lord.
items.note: Waiting is hard. Be strong, take heart, and keep trusting God.

items.text: I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.
items.note: God promises to guide you and keep his eye on you. You're not walking alone.

items.text: Commit your way to the Lord. Trust also in him, and he will do this: he will make your righteousness go out as the light, and your justice as the noon day sun.
items.note: Hand your plans to God and trust him. He'll bring the right things into the light.

items.text: Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.
items.note: Slow down and be still. God is God, and you don't have to carry everything.

items.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
items.note: Your days matter. Ask God to help you use them well.

items.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. All those who do his work have a good understanding. His praise endures forever!
items.note: Respecting God is where wisdom starts, and doing what he says brings understanding.

items.text: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
items.note: Want to keep your life clean? Live by what God says.

items.text: I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
items.note: Hiding God's word in your heart helps you stand strong when temptation comes.

items.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
items.note: God's word lights up your next step, even when the road ahead is dark.

items.text: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
items.note: Ask God to look at your heart and lead you. He's gentle with what he finds.

items.text: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
items.note: Start your day by trusting God's love and asking him which way to go.

items.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
items.note: Real joy is found with God. He shows you the path of life.

items.text: Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
items.note: Whatever you're carrying, hand it to God. He'll hold you up.

items.text: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
items.note: When you need help, look up. Your help comes from the one who made everything.

items.text: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’
items.note: Honoring God and turning from evil is what wisdom really is.

items.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the Lord require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
items.note: God's ask is simple: do what's right, love mercy, and walk humbly with him.

items.text: Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
items.note: Hearing Jesus and doing what he says is like building your life on solid rock.

items.text: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things.
items.note: What you think about matters. Fill your mind with what's true, good and beautiful.

items.text: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
items.note: Being young doesn't mean you can't lead. Set the example in how you talk and live.

items.text: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
items.note: Let your words be kind and thoughtful, so people want to hear more.

items.text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
items.note: Bad company changes good people. Choose friends who make you better.

items.text: Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
items.note: Don't let evil win by making you bitter. Beat it by doing good.

items.text: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
items.note: Before you say it, ask: will this build them up? If not, skip it.

items.text: Flee from youthful lusts; but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
items.note: Run from what pulls you down, and run toward God with friends who love him.

items.text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
items.note: No temptation is too big for you with God. He always gives you a way out.

items.text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
items.note: Tomorrow can wait. Focus on today and trust God with the rest.
